text:
𝗧𝗵𝗲 Snowflake 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗼𝗱𝗶𝗰 𝗧𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 ❄️

A simple visual map of the capabilities that make up a modern Snowflake ecosystem.
You can think of it in 7 major layers:

• 𝗜𝗻𝗴𝗲𝘀𝘁 → COPY INTO, Snowpipe, Streaming, Openflow, Connectors 
• 𝗦𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗲 → Tables, Stages, Hybrid Tables, File Formats, Cloning 
• 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗰𝗲𝘀𝘀 → SQL, Snowpark, Dynamic Tables, Streams, Tasks, dbt 
• 𝗚𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗻 → RBAC, Masking, Row Access Policies, Tags, Auditing 
• 𝗔𝗻𝗮𝗹𝘆𝘇𝗲 → Snowsight, Worksheets, Dashboards, Collaboration 
• 𝗕𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱 𝗔𝗜 → Cortex, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, Agents, Snowpark ML 
• 𝗦𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗲 → Listings, Marketplace, Native Apps, Data Sharing, Integrations

The interesting part is not the number of features.

It is how these capabilities connect.

𝗜𝗻𝗴𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 without governance creates chaos. 

𝗔𝗜 without trusted data creates unreliable outcomes. 

𝗔𝗻𝗮𝗹𝘆𝘁𝗶𝗰𝘀 without context creates weak decisions. 

𝗦𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 without security creates risk.

The real value comes when the platform works as one connected system.
𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮 → 𝗚𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 → 𝗔𝗻𝗮𝗹𝘆𝘁𝗶𝗰𝘀 → 𝗔𝗜 → 𝗔𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

That is where modern data platforms are heading.
Not more tools.

𝗕𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗲𝘅𝘁. 
𝗕𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗴𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻. 
𝗕𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗴𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲.

author: Sumanth P
headline: Founder & CEO @ Devable | Building growth engines for AI-native devtools & platforms | LLMs, RAG, AI Agents | AI Engineering
text:
Microsoft open-sourced an AI Engineer Coach!

AI Engineer Coach is a VS Code extension that reads your local AI coding session logs and turns them into actionable insights. Works with any harness - Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, Codex, Cline. Everything runs on your machine. No data leaves.

Most developers using AI coding tools don't know if they're actually getting better at using them. What prompts they repeat. What habits are slowing them down. What their context health looks like. This extension answers all of that.

Four layers:

1. Observe - Practice scores with week-over-week trends, daily activity charts, Gantt-style session timeline, and a screenshot gallery from your coding sessions.

2. Measure - AI-generated code volume broken down by language, model, workspace, and harness. Activity heatmaps showing your 7×24 coding patterns.

3. Improve - 45 anti-pattern rules across prompt quality, session hygiene, code review, tool mastery, and context management. Each rule comes with severity ratings and concrete actions. Skill Finder discovers repeated prompt patterns and matches them to reusable skills from the open-source catalog. Context Health runs agentic readiness checks and audits your instruction files.

4. Level Up - Personalized quizzes generated from your actual usage data. XP-based progression with Bronze to Diamond tiers. An Agentic SDLC view showing how you use AI across the full development lifecycle.

Key capabilities:

• Works with any AI coding harness in one dashboard
• 45 anti-pattern detection rules across 5 categories
• Skill Finder for repeated prompts and reusable skills
• Context Health with agentic readiness checks
• Personalized quizzes from your actual session data
• All local - no data leaves your machine
• Editable rules with live testing via Rule Playground

100% open source.

I've shared the link in the replies!

author: Rajat Garg
headline: Founder, CEO at Bosscoder | Building the Future of Tech Education in India | Ex-Microsoft
text:
Here is how my interview at Amazon for SDE went (36 LPA)👇

This was an on-campus Amazon interview, and every round eventually came down to the same core skills:

📍 Round 1: Online Coding Round
2 DSA coding problems + MCQs on DBMS, code output, etc.

📍 Round 2: 1:1 DSA Interview
2 coding problems focused on Binary Search and Greedy logic.

📍 Round 3: 1:1 DSA Interview
Problems around Maximum Subarray and Binary Search.

📍 Round 4: Managerial Round 
Started with a simple DSA question, followed by a deep discussion on one project and behavioral questions like “Why Amazon?” and “How do you learn?”

Out of all candidates, only 3 were selected, and I was fortunate to be one of them.

I eventually chose Microsoft over Amazon, but this interview made one thing very clear to me:

👉 Top product companies test the same fundamentals, again and again.
DSA, problem-solving depth, CS basics, projects, and communication, not random tricks.

This insight is one of the biggest reasons Bosscoder Academy exists today.

headline: 🚀 44k+ LinkedIns ✅ Open For Collabs🤝|☁️ AWS Data Engineer 🚀| AI | AWS(5+ yr) | | Python · PySpark · Pandas . AWS (S3, Redshift, Glue, Athena)
text:
🚀 Great news for Data Engineers preparing for top product & consulting companies!

If you're aiming for companies like EY, Flipkart, or any top-tier data role — mastering advanced SQL is a game changer.

I recently came across some powerful SQL interview concepts, and honestly… this is where average candidates get filtered out and strong candidates stand out 👇

💡 Here’s what top companies are really testing:

🔹 Window Functions vs GROUP BY 
Do you just aggregate data… or can you derive insights without losing granularity?

🔹 CTE vs Subquery Performance 
Writing queries is easy. Writing optimized, readable, and scalable queries is what matters.

🔹 Indexing Strategy for Large Tables 
Anyone can query data. But can you design for 1TB+ scale performance?

🔹 Recursive CTE (Hierarchy Problems) 
Real-world data isn’t flat. Think org structures, category trees, graphs.

🔹 MERGE (Upsert) in Data Warehousing 
This is not just SQL — this is real production mindset (SCD Type 2, atomicity, consistency).

🔹 Handling NULLs in Aggregations 
Small detail… BIG impact on data accuracy.

🔹 Query Plan Analysis 
Top engineers don’t guess — they read execution plans and optimize smartly.
🔥 Reality check:
Most people prepare SQL at a basic level.

But interviews at top companies? 
They expect you to think like a Data Engineer in production, not just a query writer.
💬 If you're preparing for Data Engineering roles (5–7 years level), focus on:

✔ Optimization mindset 
✔ Real-world scenarios 
✔ Clean & scalable SQL 
✔ Understanding "WHY", not just "HOW"
